decisive_items: repeated right-sided epistaxis without obvious trauma
Multiple small capillary malformations on trunk (hyperpigmented)
response.rationale: The patient's symptoms of repeated epistaxis, capillary malformations, and vascular malformation are most consistent with Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia (R1), although Sturge-Weber syndrome (R5) is also a possible diagnosis due to the presence of capillary malformations and erythema.

rejected.why: Lack of specific vascular malformations and more characteristic features of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
Klippel-Trenaunay-Weber syndrome typically presents with more pronounced limb hypertrophy and port-wine stains
PHACE syndrome is less likely due to the absence of more characteristic features such as large facial hemangiomas
